<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

fs3-parsers owns grammar selection (`Language`) and the generic walk (`source.rs`); fs3-core owns `classify`. Adding TypeScript is: a grammar crate + two Language variants + extension mapping (lib.rs), plus classify decisions for TypeScript node kinds. The only new mechanism is a value-shape rule in the generic walk: a binding node (`variable_declarator`, `public_field_definition`) whose `value` child is a function-like node classifies as Function and takes the binding's name — written without a language branch so it also serves JavaScript later. Nothing downstream (store, embeddings, CLI) changes: element kinds, addresses and spans are the existing contract.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| risk-1 | tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 may pin an older tree-sitter ABI than 0.26 — t1 proves it or stops |
| risk-2 | classify is heuristic on substrings: `type_alias_declaration` and `internal_module` ride on 'type'/'mod' hints — write the tests so a future hint change fails loudly |
| risk-3 | the value-shape rule could double-emit or emit for non-function values — the fixture must include `const x = 1` and `const cfg = {}` as negatives |
| risk-4 | TSX JSX error-recovery nodes may carry empty names — first_identifier_text already drops blank names; assert no `&lt;anonymous&gt;`/empty-address elements |
